items.stem: State any three qualities that make an accounting principle generally accepted.
items.answer: Relevance; Objectivity; Feasibility
items.markingKey: Any three of: Relevance; Objectivity; Feasibility (1 mark each).

items.stem: Which of the following statements about Generally Accepted Accounting Principles is correct?
items.answer: A principle should be relevant, objective and feasible to be generally accepted.
items.markingKey: (c) Correct: A principle should be relevant, objective and feasible to be generally accepted.
options: GAAP apply only to sole proprietorships.
Every firm is free to adopt its own principles for its published accounts.
A principle should be relevant, objective and feasible to be generally accepted.
GAAP are natural laws that never change.

items.stem: A proposed rule would require Mehta Industries to value every item of stock daily by an outside valuer, which is too costly for a small stationery shop. Which quality required of a generally accepted accounting principle is missing?
items.answer: Feasibility
items.markingKey: (a) Feasibility. A principle must be practicable without undue complexity or cost.

items.stem: A proposed rule lets the owner of Joshi Agencies value assets at whatever figure he personally thinks fair. Which quality required of a generally accepted accounting principle is missing? Justify your answer.
items.answer: Objectivity. A principle must be free from personal bias and based on facts.
items.markingKey: 1 mark for identifying Objectivity; 2 marks for the justification: A principle must be free from personal bias and based on facts.

items.stem:
Jain Industries and Menon Agencies are two kitchen appliances firms in Pune. Jain Industries values its closing stock at cost while Menon Agencies values it at selling price. An investor Karthik wants to compare their profits.
(i) Why will Karthik find the comparison misleading? (ii) How do GAAP and accounting standards solve this problem?
items.answer: (i) The two firms use different principles for the same item, so their profits are not computed on the same basis. (ii) They lay down uniform rules (stock at cost or net realisable value, whichever is lower), bringing uniformity and comparability.
items.markingKey: 4 marks: (i) The two firms use different principles for the same item, so their profits are not computed on the same basis. (ii) They lay down uniform rules (stock at cost or net realisable value, whichever is lower), bringing uniformity and comparability.

items.stem: Which term is described here? "The fundamental ideas or basic assumptions underlying the theory and practice of financial accounting."
items.answer: Basic accounting concepts
items.markingKey: (c) Basic accounting concepts: The fundamental ideas or basic assumptions underlying the theory and practice of financial accounting.

items.stem: Explain the following reasons why GAAP are needed: (i) Reliability for users (ii) Basis for accounting standards and law.
items.answer: (i) Reliability for users: Users can depend on statements prepared on accepted principles. (ii) Basis for accounting standards and law: Standards and legal requirements build on accepted principles.
items.markingKey: 2 marks each: (i) Users can depend on statements prepared on accepted principles. (ii) Standards and legal requirements build on accepted principles.

items.stem: Which quality required of a generally accepted accounting principle is missing? In each case give a reason. (i) A proposed rule would require Mishra Industries to value every item of stock daily by an outside valuer, which is too costly for a small electronic goods shop. (ii) A proposed rule would make Mishra Industries report the number of tea breaks taken by staff, which no user needs.
items.answer: (i) Feasibility: A principle must be practicable without undue complexity or cost. (ii) Relevance: A principle must produce information that is useful to users.
items.markingKey: 2 marks each (1 identification + 1 reason): (i) Feasibility (ii) Relevance

items.stem: Which of the following best describes "Cost concept"?
items.answer: Assets are recorded at the price paid to acquire them, and this cost is the basis for all later accounting for the asset.
items.markingKey: (d) Cost concept: Assets are recorded at the price paid to acquire them, and this cost is the basis for all later accounting for the asset.
options: The business is treated as separate and distinct from its owner, so transactions are recorded from the point of view of the business.
Only those transactions and events that can be expressed in terms of money are recorded in the books.
The business is assumed to continue its operations for a long period and not to be wound up in the near future.
Assets are recorded at the price paid to acquire them, and this cost is the basis for all later accounting for the asset.

items.stem: State one difference between business entity concept and money measurement concept on the basis of meaning.
items.answer: business entity concept: the business is separate from its owner; money measurement concept: only money-measurable events are recorded
items.markingKey: 1 mark: business entity concept: the business is separate from its owner; money measurement concept: only money-measurable events are recorded

items.stem: Distinguish between business entity concept and money measurement concept on the basis of purpose, meaning and example.
items.answer: (i) Purpose: business entity concept: to find the true profit of the business, not of the owner; money measurement concept: to express dissimilar items in a common unit. (ii) Meaning: business entity concept: the business is separate from its owner; money measurement concept: only money-measurable events are recorded. (iii) Example: business entity concept: owner's personal expenses paid by the business are drawings; money measurement concept: skill of employees is not recorded.
items.markingKey: 1 mark for each basis: (i) Purpose: business entity concept: to find the true profit of the business, not of the owner; money measurement concept: to express dissimilar items in a common unit. (ii) Meaning: business entity concept: the business is separate from its owner; money measurement concept: only money-measurable events are recorded. (iii) Example: business entity concept: owner's personal expenses paid by the business are drawings; money measurement concept: skill of employees is not recorded.

items.stem: Goyal Enterprises prepares its profit and loss account for the year 1 April to 31 March every year. Which accounting concept is applied?
items.answer: Accounting period concept
items.markingKey: (a) Accounting period concept. The life of the business is divided into periods of one year.

items.stem: Rao and Sons bought a machine for ₹4,00,000 expected to last 10 years and charges depreciation every year instead of treating the whole cost as this year's expense. Which accounting concept is applied? Justify your answer.
items.answer: Going concern concept. Because the business will continue, the cost is spread over the useful life.
items.markingKey: 1 mark for identifying Going concern concept; 2 marks for the justification: Because the business will continue, the cost is spread over the useful life.

items.stem: Which accounting concept is applied? In each case give a reason. (i) Prepaid insurance of Verma Stores is shown as an asset because the business is expected to use the benefit next year. (ii) Goods bought for ₹30,000 on credit increase stock by ₹30,000 and creditors by ₹30,000.
items.answer: (i) Going concern concept: The business is assumed to continue, so future benefits are carried forward. (ii) Dual aspect concept: Both aspects of the transaction are recorded for equal amounts.
items.markingKey: 2 marks each (1 identification + 1 reason): (i) Going concern concept (ii) Dual aspect concept

items.stem:
Rahul owns Ahuja Brothers in Mumbai. During March: (a) he paid his daughter's college fees of ₹45,000 from the business bank account; (b) the business bought a building for ₹40 lakh, now worth ₹48 lakh; (c) the shop's friendly location is a big advantage but is not recorded.
(i) Name the concept involved in each of (a), (b) and (c). (ii) How should (a) and (b) be shown in the books?
items.answer: (i) (a) Business entity concept (b) Cost concept (c) Money measurement concept. (ii) (a) As drawings, reducing his capital (Drawings A/c Dr To Bank A/c ₹45,000). (b) Building at its cost of ₹40 lakh (less depreciation), not ₹48 lakh.
items.markingKey: 4 marks: (i) (a) Business entity concept (b) Cost concept (c) Money measurement concept. (ii) (a) As drawings, reducing his capital (Drawings A/c Dr To Bank A/c ₹45,000). (b) Building at its cost of ₹40 lakh (less depreciation), not ₹48 lakh.

items.stem:
Farhan owns Rao Traders in Shimla. During March: (a) he paid his daughter's college fees of ₹45,000 from the business bank account; (b) the business bought a building for ₹40 lakh, now worth ₹48 lakh; (c) the shop's friendly location is a big advantage but is not recorded.
(i) Name the concept involved in each of (a), (b) and (c). (ii) How should (a) and (b) be shown in the books?
items.answer: (i) (a) Business entity concept (b) Cost concept (c) Money measurement concept. (ii) (a) As drawings, reducing his capital (Drawings A/c Dr To Bank A/c ₹45,000). (b) Building at its cost of ₹40 lakh (less depreciation), not ₹48 lakh.
items.markingKey: 4 marks: (i) (a) Business entity concept (b) Cost concept (c) Money measurement concept. (ii) (a) As drawings, reducing his capital (Drawings A/c Dr To Bank A/c ₹45,000). (b) Building at its cost of ₹40 lakh (less depreciation), not ₹48 lakh.

items.stem: Which accounting concept is described here? "The life of the business is divided into smaller periods, usually a year, at the end of which results and position are ascertained."
items.answer: Accounting period concept
items.markingKey: (a) Accounting period concept: The life of the business is divided into smaller periods, usually a year, at the end of which results and position are ascertained.

items.stem: Which of the following statements about basic accounting concepts is NOT correct?
items.answer: Under the money measurement concept, the health of the manager is recorded in the books.
items.markingKey: (d) Incorrect statement: Under the money measurement concept, the health of the manager is recorded in the books.
options: The money measurement concept excludes events that cannot be measured in money.
The dual aspect concept is the basis of the accounting equation.
The going concern concept justifies charging depreciation over the life of an asset.
Under the money measurement concept, the health of the manager is recorded in the books.

items.stem: Which of the following statements about basic accounting concepts is correct?
items.answer: Under the cost concept assets are recorded at their acquisition cost.
items.markingKey: (a) Correct: Under the cost concept assets are recorded at their acquisition cost.
options: Under the cost concept assets are recorded at their acquisition cost.
The cost concept requires assets to be revalued every year at market price.
The accounting period concept assumes the business will be closed at the end of each year.
Under the money measurement concept, the health of the manager is recorded in the books.

items.stem: Which of the following is true of business entity concept but not of money measurement concept?
items.answer: Example: owner's personal expenses paid by the business are drawings
items.markingKey: (b) business entity concept: Example: owner's personal expenses paid by the business are drawings. The other options describe money measurement concept.
options: Purpose: to express dissimilar items in a common unit
Example: owner's personal expenses paid by the business are drawings
Meaning: only money-measurable events are recorded
Example: skill of employees is not recorded

items.stem:
Kavya, a new accountant at Verma Enterprises, suggests three changes: (i) record the building at its present market value every year; (ii) show the proprietor's house rent as a business expense since the proprietor is the business; (iii) charge the entire cost of a 10-year machine to this year's profit.
(i) Which concept does each suggestion violate? (ii) Explain the correct treatment in each case. (iii) What would happen to the reported profit if all three were accepted?
items.answer: (i) (i) Cost concept (ii) Business entity concept (iii) Going concern concept (and matching). (ii) (i) Show the building at cost less depreciation. (ii) Treat the house rent as drawings. (iii) Spread the cost over 10 years by charging depreciation. (iii) Profit would be distorted: understated by the full machine cost and the house rent, and asset values would fluctuate with the market, so statements would be unreliable and not comparable.
items.markingKey: 6 marks: (i) (i) Cost concept (ii) Business entity concept (iii) Going concern concept (and matching). (ii) (i) Show the building at cost less depreciation. (ii) Treat the house rent as drawings. (iii) Spread the cost over 10 years by charging depreciation. (iii) Profit would be distorted: understated by the full machine cost and the house rent, and asset values would fluctuate with the market, so statements would be unreliable and not comparable.

items.stem: What is meant by "Matching concept"?
items.answer: Expenses incurred in a period are set against the revenues earned in that same period to find the profit.
items.markingKey: 1 mark: Expenses incurred in a period are set against the revenues earned in that same period to find the profit.

items.stem: Which of the following is true of consistency concept but not of conservatism concept?
items.answer: Meaning: the same methods are followed year after year
items.markingKey: (d) consistency concept: Meaning: the same methods are followed year after year. The other options describe conservatism concept.
options: Example: valuing stock at cost or market price, whichever is lower
Purpose: to avoid overstating profit and assets
Meaning: anticipate no profit but provide for all possible losses
Meaning: the same methods are followed year after year

items.stem: Distinguish between consistency concept and conservatism concept on the basis of purpose, example and meaning.
items.answer: (i) Purpose: consistency concept: to make results of different periods comparable; conservatism concept: to avoid overstating profit and assets. (ii) Example: consistency concept: continuing the same depreciation method every year; conservatism concept: valuing stock at cost or market price, whichever is lower. (iii) Meaning: consistency concept: the same methods are followed year after year; conservatism concept: anticipate no profit but provide for all possible losses.
items.markingKey: 1 mark for each basis: (i) Purpose: consistency concept: to make results of different periods comparable; conservatism concept: to avoid overstating profit and assets. (ii) Example: consistency concept: continuing the same depreciation method every year; conservatism concept: valuing stock at cost or market price, whichever is lower. (iii) Meaning: consistency concept: the same methods are followed year after year; conservatism concept: anticipate no profit but provide for all possible losses.

items.stem: Sethi Industries delivered goods worth ₹80,000 to a customer on 28 March; payment will be received in May. The sale is recorded in March. Which accounting concept is followed?
items.answer: Revenue recognition concept
items.markingKey: (b) Revenue recognition concept. Revenue is recognised when the sale is made, not when cash is received.

items.stem: Joshi Stores shows its debtors, creditors, loans and contingent liabilities separately in the balance sheet with notes. Which accounting concept is followed? Justify your answer.
items.answer: Full disclosure concept. Complete and material information is disclosed.
items.markingKey: 1 mark for identifying Full disclosure concept; 2 marks for the justification: Complete and material information is disclosed.

items.stem:
The accountant of Nair Traders, Bhopal, (a) recorded as sales an order of ₹2,00,000 received on 30 March for delivery in May; (b) changed from the written down value method to the straight line method without any reason, increasing profit; (c) did not mention in the accounts a large claim filed against the firm.
(i) Identify the concept violated in each case. (ii) State the correct treatment of (a).
items.answer: (i) (a) Revenue recognition (b) Consistency (c) Full disclosure. (ii) The order is not a sale; revenue is recognised in May when goods are delivered (right to receive arises).
items.markingKey: 4 marks: (i) (a) Revenue recognition (b) Consistency (c) Full disclosure. (ii) The order is not a sale; revenue is recognised in May when goods are delivered (right to receive arises).

items.stem: Which of the following statements about accounting concepts is NOT correct?
items.answer: Conservatism allows a business to record expected profits.
items.markingKey: (a) Incorrect statement: Conservatism allows a business to record expected profits.
options: Conservatism allows a business to record expected profits.
Objectivity requires transactions to be supported by verifiable evidence.
Consistency improves the comparability of financial statements.
Conservatism means providing for all possible losses but not anticipating profits.

items.stem:
Aarav, owner of Sethi Brothers, expects the price of the stock lying in his godown to rise by 20% next month and wants to show the expected gain as this year's profit. He also does not want to provide for a debtor who has become insolvent.
(i) Which concept is he ignoring? Explain it. (ii) Advise him on both points.
items.answer: (i) Conservatism (prudence): anticipate no profit but provide for all possible losses. (ii) Do not record the expected price rise; value stock at cost or net realisable value, whichever is lower. Write off or provide for the doubtful debt.
items.markingKey: 4 marks: (i) Conservatism (prudence): anticipate no profit but provide for all possible losses. (ii) Do not record the expected price rise; value stock at cost or net realisable value, whichever is lower. Write off or provide for the doubtful debt.

items.stem: Which accounting concept is described here? "Accounting transactions are recorded in an objective manner, free from personal bias, and are supported by verifiable documents."
items.answer: Objectivity concept
items.markingKey: (b) Objectivity concept: Accounting transactions are recorded in an objective manner, free from personal bias, and are supported by verifiable documents.

items.stem: Which of the following statements about accounting concepts is correct?
items.answer: Consistency improves the comparability of financial statements.
items.markingKey: (c) Correct: Consistency improves the comparability of financial statements.
options: Conservatism allows a business to record expected profits.
Consistency means changing methods every year to suit the situation.
Consistency improves the comparability of financial statements.
Under revenue recognition, a credit sale is recorded only when payment is received.

items.stem: Which of the following best describes "IFRS"?
items.answer: International Financial Reporting Standards issued by the International Accounting Standards Board (IASB).
items.markingKey: (d) IFRS: International Financial Reporting Standards issued by the International Accounting Standards Board (IASB).
options: Entries are made only when cash is received or paid, so revenues and expenses are recorded in the period of receipt or payment.
Written policy documents issued by an expert accounting body or the government covering recognition, measurement, presentation and disclosure of transactions.
Revenues and costs are recorded in the period in which they are earned or incurred, whether or not cash is received or paid.
International Financial Reporting Standards issued by the International Accounting Standards Board (IASB).

items.stem: Which of the following is NOT one of the benefits of accounting standards?
items.answer: Rigidity
items.markingKey: (d) "Rigidity" is one of the limitations of accounting standards, not one of the benefits of accounting standards.

items.stem: Reddy Enterprises received commission of ₹1,88,000 in cash during the year. Of this, ₹15,000 relates to next year. Commission of ₹25,000 earned this year has not yet been received. What commission is credited to the profit and loss account under the accrual basis?
Iyer Industries shows commission earned but not yet received as income of the current year. Which basis of accounting is followed? Justify your answer.
items.answer: Accrual basis of accounting. Income is recorded when earned.
items.markingKey: 1 mark for identifying Accrual basis of accounting; 2 marks for the justification: Income is recorded when earned.

items.stem: Harleen, a chartered accountant in Coimbatore, received fees of ₹7,75,000 during the year, which include ₹46,000 received in advance for next year. Fees of ₹65,000 earned this year are still to be received. Expenses paid were ₹3,65,000 and expenses of ₹19,000 are outstanding. Find the profit under (i) the cash basis (ii) the accrual basis.

Sneha, a chartered accountant in Mumbai, received fees of ₹5,35,000 during the year, which include ₹29,000 received in advance for next year. Fees of ₹39,000 earned this year are still to be received. Expenses paid were ₹2,15,000 and expenses of ₹14,000 are outstanding. Find the profit under (i) the cash basis (ii) the accrual basis.
A small tuition centre run by Manish records only money actually received from students and actual payments made. Which basis of accounting is followed?
items.answer: Cash basis of accounting
items.markingKey: (d) Cash basis of accounting. Entries are made only on receipt or payment of cash.

items.stem: Tara, a chartered accountant in Jaipur, received fees of ₹3,95,000 during the year, which include ₹20,000 received in advance for next year. Fees of ₹50,000 earned this year are still to be received. Expenses paid were ₹1,95,000 and expenses of ₹51,000 are outstanding. Find the profit under (i) the cash basis (ii) the accrual basis.

Kabir, a chartered accountant in Bhopal, received fees of ₹4,65,000 during the year, which include ₹21,000 received in advance for next year. Fees of ₹82,000 earned this year are still to be received. Expenses paid were ₹2,20,000 and expenses of ₹18,000 are outstanding. Find the profit under (i) the cash basis (ii) the accrual basis.
State any three features of GST.
items.answer: One nation, one tax; Destination-based tax; Dual GST; Input tax credit across the chain; IGST on inter-state supplies; Online compliance through GSTN
items.markingKey: Any three of: One nation, one tax; Destination-based tax; Dual GST; Input tax credit across the chain; IGST on inter-state supplies; Online compliance through GSTN (1 mark each).

items.stem: Which of the following statements about Goods and Services Tax is correct?
items.answer: Input tax credit of IGST can be used against IGST, CGST and SGST payable.
items.markingKey: (d) Correct: Input tax credit of IGST can be used against IGST, CGST and SGST payable.
options: IGST is charged on supplies within the same state.
Under GST, input tax credit is not available to registered dealers.
GST is levied only by the Central Government.
Input tax credit of IGST can be used against IGST, CGST and SGST payable.

items.stem:
Assertion (A): Input CGST can be set off against output SGST.
Reason (R): CGST and SGST are levied by different governments.
Choose the correct option.
items.answer: A is false, but R is true.
items.markingKey: (d) A is false: CGST credit cannot be used for SGST. R is true.
options: Both A and R are true, and R is the correct explanation of A.
Both A and R are true, but R is not the correct explanation of A.
A is true, but R is false.
A is false, but R is true.

items.stem: Jain Industries of Kochi (Kerala) sends organic food products to a buyer in Chennai (Tamil Nadu). Which GST is charged on this supply?
items.answer: IGST
items.markingKey: (d) IGST. Kerala to Tamil Nadu is an inter-state supply.

items.stem: Pass the journal entry in the books of Sharma Agencies, Jaipur: purchased goods for ₹28,000 from Reddy and Sons of the same state on credit, plus CGST and SGST at 9% each.
items.answer: Purchases A/c Dr ₹28,000; Input CGST A/c Dr ₹2,520; Input SGST A/c Dr ₹2,520; To Reddy and Sons ₹33,040
items.markingKey: Purchases debited ₹28,000 (1); input CGST and SGST ₹2,520 each debited (1); supplier credited with ₹33,040 (1).

items.stem: Saxena Brothers has: output IGST ₹14,000, output CGST ₹13,000, output SGST ₹13,000; input IGST ₹35,000, input CGST ₹6,000, input SGST ₹6,000. Using the input tax credit rules (IGST credit first against IGST, then CGST, then SGST), find the net CGST and SGST payable.
items.answer: IGST nil, CGST ₹0, SGST ₹0; IGST credit of ₹7,000 carried forward
items.markingKey: IGST credit ₹35,000 − output IGST ₹14,000 = ₹21,000 left. CGST: ₹13,000 − ₹6,000 = ₹7,000, less IGST credit ₹7,000 = ₹0. SGST: ₹13,000 − ₹6,000 = ₹7,000, less remaining IGST credit ₹7,000 = ₹0; IGST credit of ₹7,000 carried forward.

items.stem: Which of the following statements about Goods and Services Tax is NOT correct?
items.answer: IGST is charged on supplies within the same state.
items.markingKey: (c) Incorrect statement: IGST is charged on supplies within the same state.
options: On an intra-state supply, CGST and SGST are charged at equal rates.
Input tax credit of IGST can be used against IGST, CGST and SGST payable.
IGST is charged on supplies within the same state.
GST was introduced in India from 1 July 2017.

items.stem: Joshi Industries of Surat (Gujarat) sells organic food products to a dealer in Ahmedabad (Gujarat). Which GST is charged on this supply? Justify your answer.
items.answer: CGST and SGST. Same state: intra-state supply.
items.markingKey: 1 mark for identifying CGST and SGST; 2 marks for the justification: Same state: intra-state supply.

items.stem: Bose Stores of Surat sold goods worth ₹2,97,000 to a buyer in another state. GST rate is 18%. Calculate the tax charged and the total invoice value.
items.markingKey: Inter-state: IGST 18% of ₹2,97,000 = ₹53,460; invoice ₹3,50,460.

items.stem: Bansal Industries of Bhopal bought goods for ₹1,55,000 and sold them for ₹1,85,000, both within the same state. GST is 18% (CGST 9% + SGST 9%). Find the CGST and SGST payable after input tax credit.
items.markingKey: Output CGST = ₹16,650, input CGST = ₹13,950, payable ₹2,700; SGST the same: ₹2,700.

items.stem: Thakur Industries creates a provision for doubtful debts at 5% on its debtors. Which accounting concept is followed? Justify your answer.
items.answer: Conservatism concept. A provision is made for possible losses.
items.markingKey: 1 mark for identifying Conservatism concept; 2 marks for the justification: A provision is made for possible losses.

items.stem: What is meant by "Accounting standards"?
items.answer: Written statements of uniform accounting rules and guidelines issued by an expert body for preparing consistent financial statements.
items.markingKey: 1 mark: Written statements of uniform accounting rules and guidelines issued by an expert body for preparing consistent financial statements.

items.stem: Explain the following limitations of accounting standards: (i) Cannot override the law (ii) Rigidity.
items.answer: (i) Cannot override the law: Standards are framed within, and cannot override, the statute. (ii) Rigidity: Standards may be rigid and not suit every situation.
items.markingKey: 2 marks each: (i) Standards are framed within, and cannot override, the statute. (ii) Standards may be rigid and not suit every situation.

items.stem: Menon Enterprises of Lucknow (Uttar Pradesh) supplies medicines to a shop in Kanpur (Uttar Pradesh). Which GST is charged on this supply?
items.answer: CGST and SGST
items.markingKey: (b) CGST and SGST. Both places are in Uttar Pradesh: intra-state supply.

items.stem:
Das Industries and Bose Traders are two kitchen appliances firms in Pune. Das Industries values its closing stock at cost while Bose Traders values it at selling price. An investor Mehak wants to compare their profits.
(i) Why will Mehak find the comparison misleading? (ii) How do GAAP and accounting standards solve this problem?
items.answer: (i) The two firms use different principles for the same item, so their profits are not computed on the same basis. (ii) They lay down uniform rules (stock at cost or net realisable value, whichever is lower), bringing uniformity and comparability.
items.markingKey: 4 marks: (i) The two firms use different principles for the same item, so their profits are not computed on the same basis. (ii) They lay down uniform rules (stock at cost or net realisable value, whichever is lower), bringing uniformity and comparability.

items.stem: Which of the following is one of the benefits of accounting standards?
items.answer: Inter-firm and intra-firm comparison
items.markingKey: (b) "Inter-firm and intra-firm comparison" is one of the benefits of accounting standards; the others are limitations of accounting standards.

items.stem: Lakshmi paid her personal electricity bill from the cash of Reddy Traders. The amount is recorded as drawings, not as a business expense. Which accounting concept is applied?
items.answer: Business entity concept
items.markingKey: (d) Business entity concept. The owner and the business are separate; personal payments are drawings.

items.stem:
Assertion (A): Revenue is recognised only when cash is received.
Reason (R): Revenue is recognised when the right to receive it is established.
Choose the correct option.
items.answer: A is false, but R is true.
items.markingKey: (d) A is false: revenue recognition does not wait for cash. R is true.
options: Both A and R are true, and R is the correct explanation of A.
Both A and R are true, but R is not the correct explanation of A.
A is true, but R is false.

items.stem: Sharma Retail of Delhi sold goods worth ₹2,31,000 to a buyer in the same state. GST rate is 5%. Calculate the CGST, SGST and the total invoice value.

Assertion (A): Capital is shown as a liability in the books of the business.
Reason (R): According to the business entity concept, the owner and the business are separate.
Choose the correct option.
items.answer: Both A and R are true, and R is the correct explanation of A.
items.markingKey: (a) Both true and R explains A.
options: Both A and R are true, and R is the correct explanation of A.
Both A and R are true, but R is not the correct explanation of A.
A is true, but R is false.
A is false, but R is true.

items.stem:
The accountant of Thakur and Sons, Chandigarh, (a) recorded as sales an order of ₹2,00,000 received on 30 March for delivery in May; (b) changed from the written down value method to the straight line method without any reason, increasing profit; (c) did not mention in the accounts a large claim filed against the firm.
(i) Identify the concept violated in each case. (ii) State the correct treatment of (a).
items.answer: (i) (a) Revenue recognition (b) Consistency (c) Full disclosure. (ii) The order is not a sale; revenue is recognised in May when goods are delivered (right to receive arises).
items.markingKey: 4 marks: (i) (a) Revenue recognition (b) Consistency (c) Full disclosure. (ii) The order is not a sale; revenue is recognised in May when goods are delivered (right to receive arises).

items.stem: Dr Dev, a doctor in Shimla, records fees only when patients pay, and expenses only when he pays them. Which basis of accounting is followed?
items.answer: Cash basis of accounting
items.markingKey: (d) Cash basis of accounting. Only actual cash receipts and payments are recorded.

items.stem: Explain the following features of GST: (i) IGST on inter-state supplies (ii) Destination-based tax.
items.answer: (i) IGST on inter-state supplies: The Centre collects IGST on supplies between states and shares it with the destination state. (ii) Destination-based tax: Tax accrues to the state where goods or services are consumed.
items.markingKey: 2 marks each: (i) The Centre collects IGST on supplies between states and shares it with the destination state. (ii) Tax accrues to the state where goods or services are consumed.

items.stem: Which GST term is described here? "The not-for-profit company that provides the IT infrastructure for GST registration, returns and payments."
items.answer: GSTN
items.markingKey: (b) GSTN: The not-for-profit company that provides the IT infrastructure for GST registration, returns and payments.

items.stem: A rule requires Goyal Traders to prepare a 300-page report every week, which takes more effort than its value to anyone. Which quality required of a generally accepted accounting principle is missing?
items.answer: Feasibility
items.markingKey: (d) Feasibility. The cost and effort of applying a principle must be reasonable.

items.stem: Sharma and Sons has followed the straight line method of depreciation for many years and continues it this year. Which accounting concept is followed? Justify your answer.
items.answer: Consistency concept. The same method is followed year after year.
items.markingKey: 1 mark for identifying Consistency concept; 2 marks for the justification: The same method is followed year after year.

items.stem: What is meant by "Accounting conventions"?
items.answer: Customs or practices, such as consistency and conservatism, followed by accountants because they are widely accepted.
items.markingKey: 1 mark: Customs or practices, such as consistency and conservatism, followed by accountants because they are widely accepted.

items.stem: Explain the following limitations of accounting standards: (i) Difficulty in choosing between alternatives (ii) Cannot override the law.
items.answer: (i) Difficulty in choosing between alternatives: Some standards still allow more than one treatment. (ii) Cannot override the law: Standards are framed within, and cannot override, the statute.
items.markingKey: 2 marks each: (i) Some standards still allow more than one treatment. (ii) Standards are framed within, and cannot override, the statute.

items.stem: Kulkarni Enterprises of Jaipur (Rajasthan) sells stationery to a retailer in Udaipur (Rajasthan). Which GST is charged on this supply?
items.answer: CGST and SGST
items.markingKey: (a) CGST and SGST. Seller and buyer are in the same state, so it is an intra-state supply.

items.stem:
Singh Agencies and Mehta Industries are two footwear firms in Mysuru. Singh Agencies values its closing stock at cost while Mehta Industries values it at selling price. An investor Kabir wants to compare their profits.
(i) Why will Kabir find the comparison misleading? (ii) How do GAAP and accounting standards solve this problem?
items.answer: (i) The two firms use different principles for the same item, so their profits are not computed on the same basis. (ii) They lay down uniform rules (stock at cost or net realisable value, whichever is lower), bringing uniformity and comparability.
items.markingKey: 4 marks: (i) The two firms use different principles for the same item, so their profits are not computed on the same basis. (ii) They lay down uniform rules (stock at cost or net realisable value, whichever is lower), bringing uniformity and comparability.

items.stem: Which of the following is one of the benefits of accounting standards?
items.answer: Reliability of financial statements
items.markingKey: (b) "Reliability of financial statements" is one of the benefits of accounting standards; the others are limitations of accounting standards.

items.stem: The bank wants the results of Mishra Retail every year, not only when the business closes. Which accounting concept is applied?
items.answer: Accounting period concept
items.markingKey: (b) Accounting period concept. Results are measured for regular periods for users' needs.

items.stem:
Assertion (A): A small item like a pencil sharpener is treated as an expense.
Reason (R): According to the materiality concept, items too small to influence decisions need not be treated strictly.
Choose the correct option.
items.answer: Both A and R are true, and R is the correct explanation of A.
items.markingKey: (a) Both true and R explains A.
options: Both A and R are true, and R is the correct explanation of A.
Both A and R are true, but R is not the correct explanation of A.
A is true, but R is false.
A is false, but R is true.

items.stem: Joshi Industries of Lucknow sold goods worth ₹2,49,000 to a buyer in the same state. GST rate is 5%. Calculate the CGST, SGST and the total invoice value.

Assertion (A): Fixed assets are shown at cost less depreciation and not at their market value.
Reason (R): According to the going concern concept, fixed assets are held for use and not for sale.
Choose the correct option.
items.answer: Both A and R are true, and R is the correct explanation of A.
items.markingKey: (a) Both true and R explains A.
options: Both A and R are true, and R is the correct explanation of A.
Both A and R are true, but R is not the correct explanation of A.
A is true, but R is false.
A is false, but R is true.

items.stem:
The accountant of Bose and Sons, Guwahati, (a) recorded as sales an order of ₹2,00,000 received on 30 March for delivery in May; (b) changed from the written down value method to the straight line method without any reason, increasing profit; (c) did not mention in the accounts a large claim filed against the firm.
(i) Identify the concept violated in each case. (ii) State the correct treatment of (a).
items.answer: (i) (a) Revenue recognition (b) Consistency (c) Full disclosure. (ii) The order is not a sale; revenue is recognised in May when goods are delivered (right to receive arises).
items.markingKey: 4 marks: (i) (a) Revenue recognition (b) Consistency (c) Full disclosure. (ii) The order is not a sale; revenue is recognised in May when goods are delivered (right to receive arises).

items.stem: Iyer Brothers shows commission earned but not yet received as income of the current year. Which basis of accounting is followed?
items.answer: Accrual basis of accounting
items.markingKey: (b) Accrual basis of accounting. Income is recorded when earned.

items.stem: Explain the following features of GST: (i) Online compliance through GSTN (ii) Input tax credit across the chain.
items.answer: (i) Online compliance through GSTN: Registration, returns and payments are made online. (ii) Input tax credit across the chain: Tax paid on inputs is set off, removing the cascading (tax on tax) effect.
items.markingKey: 2 marks each: (i) Registration, returns and payments are made online. (ii) Tax paid on inputs is set off, removing the cascading (tax on tax) effect.

items.stem: Which GST term is described here? "Credit for the GST paid on purchases (inputs) that a registered dealer can set off against the GST payable on sales."
items.answer: Input tax credit
items.markingKey: (b) Input tax credit: Credit for the GST paid on purchases (inputs) that a registered dealer can set off against the GST payable on sales.

items.stem: A proposed rule lets the owner of Ahuja Stores value assets at whatever figure he personally thinks fair. Which quality required of a generally accepted accounting principle is missing?
items.answer: Objectivity
items.markingKey: (d) Objectivity. A principle must be free from personal bias and based on facts.
